excludes: End-to-end RAG ingestion/retrieval/generation is owned by rag-pipeline.
General lexical/search UI implementation is owned by search-implementation.
Relational schema design without vector retrieval is owned by data-modeling.
native_ownership.responsibility: Design and implement evaluated vector retrieval with versioned embeddings/schema/index, in-query tenant authorization, deterministic lifecycle/deletion and measured recall-latency-cost migration.

reference_routing.prompt: The selected vector store and index must be evaluated for a multi-tenant corpus. Define installed-version provider filtering, index tuning, versioned embedding compatibility, reindex/cutover, deletion and recall-latency-cost evidence.
Handle a routine vector database request using only the concise main workflow; no selected provider, index, workflow-pattern, or optional deep-dive detail is needed.

risk.rationale: vector-database can change production data, model, media, security, retrieval or financial behavior and requires explicit scope, rollback and affected-path verification.

negative.prompt: Build the complete RAG pipeline including document ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector retrieval, reranking, prompt grounding, citations and no-answer behavior.
Implement product search UX and lexical/full-text query behavior, filters, pagination, highlighting and relevance without embedding infrastructure.

positive.prompt: Implement the vector-storage and similarity-retrieval layer for an existing pipeline whose document ingestion, chunking, reranking, prompting and generation remain unchanged. Use server-derived in-query tenant filters, stable source/chunk IDs, embedding/index versions, permission-change handling and verifiable source/tenant deletion.
Migrate embedding model and vector index generation using backfill, shadow/dual-read evaluation, compatible query routing, reversible cutover and measured filtered recall/latency/cost evidence.

assertions.criterion: Implements vector storage, index and retrieval lifecycle without implementing or claiming ownership of end-to-end RAG, general search or relational modeling.
Inspects corpus/queries/judgments, embedding/preprocessing/chunk/filter versions, provider/client pins, tenant auth, lifecycle/deletion, scale and tests from the fixture.
Establishes lexical/exact baseline and evaluation set, defines compatibility/tenant/lifecycle contract, then selects/tunes provider/index and plans reversible migration.

Derives tenant/resource scope server-side inside every query/write/delete, rejects embedding/schema mismatch, uses stable IDs, migrates via separate generations and propagates deletion to queues/caches/old indexes/backups.

Measures filtered recall against judgments/exact baseline plus latency percentiles/cost, tests missing filters/horizontal access, stale/missing vectors, dimension mismatch, partial backfill, cutover/rollback and verifiable deletion.

Reports the baseline/provider/index decision when evidence supports one, otherwise the decision procedure and missing evidence; reports versioned schema/lifecycle, isolation/deletion, migration and actual recall-latency-cost results or Not available, plus residual relevance/provider risk.
Keeps volatile provider APIs/defaults in the routed guide/adapter and uses immutable index generations and evaluation-derived parameters.

scenarios.prompt: A shared vector index accepts tenant ID from the client, retrieves globally then filters results in application code, mixes two embedding dimensions and deletes only the active collection. A new HNSW configuration is chosen from blog defaults without recall evidence. Repair it.

assertions.criterion: Stops retrieval for affected tenant/generations, authenticates deletion authority, tombstones stable source identities and coordinates active/old indexes, queues, caches and backups.
Rejects post-filtering as tenant security, keeps mandatory provider-side query scope and verifies deletion/retry idempotency without resurrecting vectors.
Requires negative retrieval across every generation/API, queue replay, count/source audit and documented backup erasure state rather than active-index success alone.

scenarios.prompt: A deletion request for one tenant removes source rows but leaves embeddings in an old migration index and queued retries; support proposes post-filtering queries until cleanup finishes.

assertions.criterion: Uses installed package/extension/server evidence and matching official provider/model docs; preserves the compatible tuple and treats embedding/index migration separately.
Checks client/server/index feature, embedding revision/dimensions/preprocessing/metric, metadata filter schema and backup/restore compatibility together.
Records immutable compatibility/index generation metadata and avoids remembered provider limits, dimensions, index defaults or model aliases.

scenarios.prompt: The project pins a vector client/extension and embedding model revision whose dimensions, metric and filter API differ from current examples. No migration is authorized.
